needs.why: The entire 267 MB certificate is hand-written step JSON: there is no public constructor (crates/core/src/build_support.rs is crate-private and trusted builders live only in crates/core/tests/*_builder.rs), so tools/prepare_test36_full.py imports a hand-rolled Proof step builder and adds case-specific inference writers. The chain/canonical-tuple construction is the load-bearing part: canonical_root builds 19 batches of ten prefix levels over 200 chains (longest prefix 191), decides which coordinates need integer facts (every anchor parent at a tenth level plus all 200 terminals), emits per item a flow expression, a capacity bound pair, the old row fact and an optional VarInt, then emits a local Cases with Witness branches per generated sign binary to prove each canonical coordinate equals its original continuous counterpart and to rewire every original chain row. Result: 38 SignedLift steps, 157,666 branches, 300,928 generated signed variables and rows, each SignedLift item hand-written as 4 generated variables + 4 rows.

Every added row is an exact linear combination of source rows and bound refs divided by 6: -(incident capacity rows) + sgn*balance row + 2*(flow columns with coefficient -1), i.e. C(delta(v))/6 >= ceil(|b_v|/6), then rounded by integrality of the design columns. The integer-feasible set and the objective are unchanged, the LP relaxation is strictly stronger (a complete 2,013-coordinate source point has 449/2 < 225 on round_c1). 20 added rows, 1 removed row, net 233 -> 252.

Claim 0 forward integer (source->target, projection all 2,013 coordinates, inverse present), claim 1 reverse integer, claim 2 reverse continuous (the target-LP-inside-source-LP inclusion that Strictness.inclusion_claim = 2 separates). Obligations by claim: 9,586 / 9,567 / 5,907 = 25,060, which equals the kernel's own obligations counter. Points: one complete rational source point (strictness, 52 nonzero coordinates), and integer_feasible_point plus circulation_counterexample_point each checked on the source and on the target model (52-57 nonzero entries, all others exactly zero).

test60.reformulation: Exact option-index compression of a menu/packing model. 13,550 binaries sit in 627 disjoint at-most-one rows (oneblpline, RHS 1); partitioning each group by its complete frequency coefficient vector yields exactly 1,254 blocks (two per group) whose options j=0..N satisfy a_b+j*d_b in every one of the 43 capacity coefficients and c_b+j*e_b in cost, with constant frequency coefficients and positive steps. Each block becomes one binary activation y and one bounded general integer index k with 0<=k<=N, k<=N*y; the 627 packing rows become sum_b y_b <= 1, the 46 frequency and 43 capacity definition rows become 92 lower/upper and 43 lower inequalities, and the 90 continuous auxiliaries (including obj and defblpobj) are substituted away. 13,640 vars / 717 rows -> 2,508 vars (1,254 binary + 1,254 integer) / 2,016 rows; 191,947 -> 33,494 nonzeros. The agent states the LP aggregate image is unchanged, i.e. compression, not strengthening, and claims no runtime gain (both models hit the solver time limit).

test87.reformulation: Exact staged set-cover optimization reduction, committed as runs/test87-nomf-B1/output/reformulated.mps (5,241,844 B) from input/model.mps (17,204,495 B, NAME test87): 63,009 binary columns and 507 G rows, every coefficient and RHS exactly 1, costs 1 (3,593 columns) or 2 (59,416 columns), reduced to 20,342 integer columns (20,333 unfixed + 9 FX 1) / 440 rows / 121,147 nonzeros. Three stages: fix the sole column of singleton rows to 1 (7+1+1 rows), delete rows covered by a fixed column (18+2+3) and rows whose support is contained in a retained row's (15+27+2), delete columns with empty active support (3), and replace dominated columns by a survivor with superset support and no larger cost (36,893+5,565+206 = 42,664 terminal witnesses). Later singletons (c4={x20647}, c287={x14452}) are produced BY the earlier stages. Pass 4 is a fixpoint; the incidence graph is connected in both models, so no component decomposition. Contract: forward integer NonIncreasing + reverse integer Equal, i.e. equal optimal value, not equal feasible sets.
